title: Ella Toone, Aggie Beever-Jones return to England squad for June’s World Cup qualifiers
content:
Sarina Wiegman has named a 25-player squad for England’s World Cup qualifiers against Spain and Ukraine in June.

Chelsea forward Aggie Beever-Jones and Manchester United midfielder Ella Toone both return to the squad after missing April’s international break through injury, as does London City Lionesses forward Freya Godfrey.

Goalkeeper Hannah Hampton has been included, despite being forced off with injury during Chelsea’s final Women’s Super League match of the season against Manchester United on Sunday.

Midfielder Erica Meg Parkinson, 18, who was called up to the senior side for the first time in April, is not included in June’s squad.

England play world champions Spain in Palma, Mallorca on June 5 before hosting Ukraine at Everton’s Hill Dickinson Stadium on June 9 in their final World Cup qualifier.

Wiegman’s side are top of their qualification group and can secure their place at next summer’s tournament in Brazil if they avoid defeat against Spain, having won all four of their qualifiers so far.

Analysis from football writer Cerys Jones

Wiegman’s selection largely leans on experience where possible — hardly surprising given England are looking to finish their qualifying campaign with a perfect record, and set out their stall definitively as the team to dethrone world champions Spain next summer.

After a maiden call-up in April, Ella Toone’s return from injury means that teenager Erica Meg Parkinson misses out. Double European champion Toone has not been at her dynamic best since returning for Manchester United in April, but her experience and presence in the England camp mean it would have been a shock for her not to return to the fold. Considering Aggie Beever-Jones’ limited role for Chelsea, she will be pleased to immediately recover her England place on her return from injury. Her spot among the forwards sees Jess Park named as a midfielder.

Freya Godfrey, who was forced to withdraw from April’s squad through injury, retains Wiegman’s favour and will have another chance to make her debut and establish herself as an option ahead of next summer’s tournament.

There is again no place for Grace Clinton, Grace Fisk, or Poppy Pattinson. The trio were called up in March but were not included in April’s squad, and clearly have not forced their way into Wiegman’s thinking since.

Goalkeepers: Hannah Hampton (Chelsea), Anna Moorhouse (Orlando Pride), Ellie Roebuck (Aston Villa)

Defenders: Lucy Bronze (Chelsea), Jess Carter (Gotham), Niamh Charles (Chelsea), Alex Greenwood (Manchester City), Taylor Hinds (Arsenal), Maya Le Tissier (Manchester United), Esme Morgan (Washington Spirit), Leah Williamson (Arsenal), Lotte Wubben-Moy (Arsenal)

Midfielders: Laura Blindkilde Brown (Manchester City), Lucia Kendall (Aston Villa), Jess Park (Manchester United), Georgia Stanway (Bayern Munich), Ella Toone (Manchester United), Keira Walsh (Chelsea)

Forwards: Aggie Beever-Jones (Chelsea), Freya Godfrey (London City Lionesses), Lauren Hemp (Manchester City), Lauren James (Chelsea), Chloe Kelly (Arsenal), Beth Mead (Arsenal), Alessia Russo (Arsenal)
